Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming in iOS 27, the Passwords app is getting a particularly powerful capability: it will be able to automatically change your passwords for you.

The Passwords app in iOS 27 can automatically fix compromised login accounts with your authorisation, powered by Apple Intelligence

A whole new era of Apple Intelligence is at the heart of the upcoming iOS 27 and other companion software updates. One of the powerful new AI features involves the Apple Passwords app.

The Passwords app launched two years ago as a dedicated manager for logins, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys and more.

The app has always alerted you to problems with passwords in your database. For example, if a password has appeared in a data breach or is reused across multiple accounts, the Passwords app will notify you.

But until now, you have still had to manually fix those problematic logins yourself.

However, in iOS 27, Apple says that in many cases, a new agentic AI feature can change your passwords for you automatically. According to its website:

With this feature, you can keep your logins secure, use strong passwords, and not have to put in much effort or time.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and will be released to all users in the coming weeks. The new Passwords feature is expected to ship with iOS 27.0, but rollout in the beta has been uneven, so it could slip to iOS 27.1.

Have you used the new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How has the experience been? Let us know in the comments.
